intro: PTP (Precision Time Protocol) keeps every relay and merging unit (the box that measures current and voltage) in a substation on one clock, to within a microsecond, a millionth of a second. It runs over the same Ethernet as their measurement streams, the sampled values. A grandmaster clock, locked to GPS, sends its time every second. Each switch measures how long it held the message and adds that to it, so every clock can correct for each delay on the way.
plain: The devices in a substation must agree on the time to within a millionth of a second, like singers in a choir following one conductor. A master clock, set by satellite, calls out the time every second over the network. Each network switch on the way notes how long it held the message and adds that delay to it. Every device can then take the travel time away and set its own clock exactly.

announce.title: Pick the best clock
announce.text: The GPS clock announces itself as grandmaster, the clock all others follow, once a second. It says it is locked to GPS (clock class 6) and gives its priority, 128. Every clock compares the Announce messages it hears and follows the best one.

pdelay.title: Measure the cable
pdelay.text: Every port measures the delay of its own cable, once a second. The MU (merging unit) sends a peer delay request, Pdelay_Req, at time t1. The switch gets it at t2 and answers at t3, and the MU gets the answer at t4. Delay = ((t4 − t1) − (t3 − t2)) / 2 = 1486 ns (nanoseconds). The two clocks need not agree on the time: each one only measures a difference.

sync.title: Send the time
sync.text: The grandmaster sends Sync and notes the exact moment it left. In two-step mode, that time follows in a second message, the Follow_Up. The switch passes the Sync on, and notes when it came in and when it left.

correct.title: Add the delays
correct.text: The switch is a transparent clock (TC): a switch that measures its own delay. It adds two delays to the Follow_Up's correction field: the time it held the Sync (7.436 µs) and the delay of its cable from the grandmaster (0.412 µs). The MU can now work out its offset, how far its clock is off: arrival − origin − correction − the MU's own cable delay = +2.461318 ms.

lock.title: Lock on
lock.text: The MU steps its clock back by 2.461318 ms. Then, with every Sync, it tunes how fast its clock runs. After a few seconds its offset stays under 1 µs.

sv.title: Samples in step
sv.text: The MU stamps its sampled values with the synchronized time and says so in the smpSynch field. A relay can now combine them with the samples of other merging units.

frames.announce: I am a grandmaster: class 6, locked to GPS
frames.pdelay-req: How long is our cable? (I noted t1)
frames.fup-tc: The same, plus 7848 ns spent on the way
frames.lock: Sync and Follow_Up again, every second

notes.lock: The same pair as before, with a higher sequence number. The time the switch holds a Sync differs each time, so the correction field differs too. The MU's offset is now +38 ns.
notes.sv: A sampled-values stream, not PTP: the IEC 61850 Sampled Values lesson shows its bytes. smpSynch = 2 says the samples follow a global clock, here GPS through PTP.

dst-all.name: Destination
dst-all.note: 01-1B-19-00-00-00: the multicast address for PTP over Ethernet. Transparent clocks pass it on to every port.

dst-peer.name: Destination
dst-peer.note: 01-80-C2-00-00-0E: a link-local multicast address. No switch forwards it, so Pdelay stays on one cable.

src-gm.name: Source
src-gm.note: The grandmaster's MAC address. The switch keeps it when it passes the frame on.

src-sw.name: Source
src-sw.note: The MAC address of port 3 of the switch.

ethertype.name: EtherType
ethertype.note: 0x88F7 means PTP. No IP, no UDP.

type-announce.name: Announce
type-announce.note: Low 4 bits: message type 0xB, Announce. High 4 bits: transportSpecific 0, the default.

type-pfup.name: Pdelay_Resp_Follow_Up
type-pfup.note: Message type 0xA: the follow-up to the response.

len64.name: messageLength
len64.note: 64 bytes, from the header to the end of the message.

len54.name: messageLength
len54.note: 54 bytes. All three Pdelay messages have this length.

len44.name: messageLength
len44.note: 44 bytes: the header and one timestamp.

domain.name: domainNumber
domain.note: 0, the default of IEC 61850-9-3. A clock ignores messages of another domain.

flags-announce.name: flagField
flags-announce.note: 0x003C: the UTC offset is valid, the PTP timescale is used, time and frequency are traceable (to GPS).

flags-two-step.name: flagField
flags-two-step.note: 0x0200: twoStepFlag. The exact send time follows in a second message.

corr-tc.name: correctionField
corr-tc.note: 0x1EA80000, in nanoseconds × 2^16: 7848 ns = 7436 ns in the switch + 412 ns of cable from the grandmaster.

port-gm.name: sourcePortIdentity
port-gm.note: The grandmaster's clockIdentity, made from its MAC address, and port 1. Together they name the port that sent this.

seq-announce.name: sequenceId
seq-announce.note: 0x02A7 = 679. Each message type counts on its own.

seq-fup.name: sequenceId
seq-fup.note: 0x2C1B: the same as the Sync it belongs to.

seq-pdelay.name: sequenceId
seq-pdelay.note: 0x0151 = 337. Both answers carry the number of the request.

control-other.name: controlField
control-other.note: 0x05: any other message. A field kept for PTP version 1 devices.

interval-1s.name: logMessageInterval
interval-1s.note: 0: the interval as a power of two, so one message every 2^0 = 1 s.

interval-none.name: logMessageInterval
interval-none.note: 0x7F: no fixed interval for this message.

origin-announce.name: originTimestamp
origin-announce.note: 0: an Announce may leave it empty.

utc-offset.name: currentUtcOffset
utc-offset.note: 0x0025 = 37 s. PTP counts TAI time: UTC = TAI − 37 s.

priority1.name: priority1
priority1.note: 128, compared first. The lower value wins.

class6.name: clockClass
class6.note: 6: locked to a primary reference, here GPS.

variance.name: offsetScaledLogVariance
variance.note: 0x4E5D: how steady the clock is. Lower is steadier.

gm-id.name: grandmasterIdentity
gm-id.note: The best clock this one knows: here, itself.

steps-removed.name: stepsRemoved
steps-removed.note: 0: straight from the grandmaster. Transparent clocks do not add to it.

origin-preq.name: originTimestamp
origin-preq.note: 0. The MU keeps t1, when the request left, to itself.

reserved10.name: Reserved
reserved10.note: 10 empty bytes: the request is as long as the answers.

t2.name: requestReceiptTimestamp
t2.note: t2: when the request arrived, on the switch's clock. 0x6AF597E7 s and 0x2BC1CA3A = 734120506 ns: 10:41:06.734 120 506 UTC.

t3.name: responseOriginTimestamp
t3.note: t3: when the Pdelay_Resp left the switch, 48216 ns after t2.

requesting.name: requestingPortIdentity
requesting.note: The MU's port: this answer is for it.

origin-sync.name: originTimestamp
origin-sync.note: 0. In two-step mode the exact time comes in the Follow_Up.

t-origin.name: preciseOriginTimestamp
t-origin.note: When the Sync left: 6 bytes of seconds (0x6AF597E8 = 1794480104) and 4 of nanoseconds (0x78 = 120). In TAI, so 37 s ahead of 10:41:07.000 000 120 UTC.

padding.name: Padding
padding.note: 2 bytes: an Ethernet frame needs at least 60 bytes.

a-oui.name: MAC, first half
a-oui.note: 02-00-00: the first 3 bytes of the MAC address.

a-fffe.name: FF FE
a-fffe.note: Put in the middle: a 6-byte MAC becomes an 8-byte clockIdentity.

a-nic.name: MAC, second half
a-nic.note: 00-01-01: the last 3 bytes of the MAC address.

a-port.name: portNumber
a-port.note: 1: the first port of this clock.

facts.standard: IEC/IEEE 61850-9-3 (2016) and IEEE C37.238-2017, profiles of IEEE 1588-2008 (PTP version 2)
facts.between: Grandmaster → transparent-clock switches → merging units, relays, PMUs
facts.security: None in the power profiles (the PTP settings chosen for substations): any device can announce itself as a better clock
facts.speed: Sync, Announce and Pdelay once a second; under 1 µs at every clock

tips: Every switch between the grandmaster and a clock must be a PTP transparent clock (or a boundary clock). A plain switch adds a delay that changes with the traffic, and nobody corrects it.
PTP counts TAI time, 37 s ahead of UTC. A device that ignores currentUtcOffset stamps every event 37 s off.
Check the domain number on every device. IEC 61850-9-3 uses 0 by default, IEEE C37.238-2017 uses 254, and a clock ignores messages of another domain.
PTP assumes a cable is as fast in both directions. Two fibers of different length in one link put half the difference straight into the offset.

timing.title: One Sync on its way
timing.note: Times from the moment the Sync leaves the grandmaster. The cable to the switch takes 0.412 µs, the switch holds the Sync for 7.436 µs, the cable to the MU takes 1.486 µs. The Follow_Up brings the origin time and a correction of 7.848 µs; the MU knows its own cable. What is left of arrival − origin is the error of its clock.

anatomy.port: A port identity, made from the MAC address
